title: The Board of Appeals: whose decisions stand, and who wins
question: When a permit or department decision is appealed to the Board of Appeals, how often does it stand, and does that differ by department, kind of permit, place or appellant?
finding: Of 218 appeals decided (September 2022 to November 2026), the department’s decision stood in 125 (57.3%), was changed by conditions in 65 and overturned in 28; when someone other than the holder appealed a building permit, the holder kept it unchanged in 66 of 120, had conditions added in 43 and lost it in 11. By district the share changed or overturned runs from 27.3% (District 9, 22) to 65.0% (District 8, 40; 49.9% expected from its mix of permits), and no district is beyond what chance would produce.
how: One row per appeal number. The outcome is the one in the Board’s own case report where it gives one, otherwise the last decisive action in the hearing minutes. “Changed” adds appeals granted with conditions to appeals granted outright. Who appealed is read from the minutes by comparing the appellant’s name with the name the decision was issued to: the same name means the holder appealed a decision against themselves (a denial, a penalty, a condition); a different name means a third party appealed someone else’s permit. A third party counts as an organization only when the name carries a company or association word; trusts and estates are counted as individuals. As a check, the counts of appeals denied, granted with conditions, granted and denied by default were compared with the Board’s own draft annual reports for the 3 fiscal years the minutes cover in full: they are identical in 3 (fiscal 2025: 23 denied by vote, 12 granted with conditions, 1 granted, 3 by default). Addresses are placed with the City’s address file. “Expected” gives each decided case the citywide rate for its kind of permit and kind of appellant. Because several neighbors appealing one permit each get an appeal number, the last two columns count each address and hearing once. Groups under 20 cases are left out and rates are printed only on 20 or more decided cases.
limits: The minutes read cover September 2022 to November 2026; earlier years were not obtainable. The case report gives no appellant names, so who appealed is known only for cases heard in the minutes. “Granted with conditions” can record a compromise both sides accepted, so it is not always a loss for the holder. Districts differ in how many permits are issued and in how many neighbors appeal: an area with many appeals of small alterations will show a different mix from one with few appeals of large projects. A difference between areas, or between groups of cases, is not proof of bias. Areas differ in what is proposed, in zoning, lot sizes, building ages and land prices, and in who chooses to apply, object or appeal at all.
